_doc: ASHTON dating cabinet (#14, built 2026-07-16). The easiest premium English brand to date: a REAL DATE CODE -- the suffix after 'Made in England' = 1980 + n (documented: no.3 = 1983 first year ... no.25 = 2005; used from 1983 to at least 2005). Uses the ENGINE'S EXISTING date_code channel with base_year 1980 (zero engine change -- the registry design pays off). SOURCE: staging/pipedia/Ashton.json (incl. R.D. Field's Ashton Pipe Story refs + Mike Ahmadi's 1983 stamping photos) + The_Ashton_Pipe_Story.json (mirrored).

history_anchors._doc: William 'Bill' Ashton-Taylor: joined DUNHILL 1959 at 15 (capstan lathe; mentored by Harry Saigrott on mouthpiece work) -> left in the early 1980s to found ASHTON; FIRST PIPE 1983 (only 31 pipes made that year -- rare, collectors' grail). British patent on his oil-curing method (8h heat + 8h 3-oil steep + 14 days on heated brass pegs -> 12-14% lighter pipes). Calabrian briar for smooths, Tuscan for the deep Dunhill-Shell-style blasts he revived. DIED 2009-09-16; JIMMY CRAIG continues the marque (his work for Bill dates from 2008-09; no documented stamp change -- Craig-era attribution = confirm-flow). R.D. Field = the US partner/chronicler.

brand_marks.physical: First-year 1983: simple BLOCK lettering, NO finish stamp, origin 'MADE IN LONDON ENGLAND'. Later: finish names stamped + 'Made in England' + the date-code suffix number. Sizes X, XX, XXX, LX, ELX, Magnum (magnums from Bill's personal briar privileges). Sovereign SG graded 1-5.

table.note: FIRST-YEAR origin stamp -- only used 1983 (31 pipes; block lettering, no finish stamp -- Ahmadi photos)

date_code._doc: Suffix after 'Made in England' = 1980 + n. Documented no.3 (1983) through no.25 (2005); article says 'at least up to 2002' pipes were stamped so -- post-2005 usage unverified -> a suffix >26 or absence = confirm-flow. The engine's generic runner handles it; suffixes 5-9 disambiguate via the com floor (1985-89 beat the phantom 195x candidates).

line_years._notes: 1983 pipes carried NO finish stamp ('pre-Pebble Grain' -- Ahmadi) -> any finish name = 1984+ floor. Finish names ran the brand's life; the date code does the precise work. Oak NOT encoded ('oak' = generic wood word, collision risk -> confirm-flow).

table.label: block lettering + no finish stamp = first-year 1983 profile (corroborate with MADE IN LONDON ENGLAND)

channels_future.craig_era: Jimmy Craig pipes (2008+) -- no documented stamp difference from Bill's; attribution via seller/provenance = artisan-registry career windows, confirm-flow only.
